searchText: Are any of the clients using the `minimal` style of slashing DB for slashing protection? `minimal` meaning only storing the latest attestation & block that was signed, as defined here: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3076#rationale > Whilst the format outlined in this specification is most similar to the old complete, clients who wish to follow a simpler slashing protection strategy (i.e. the old minimal), can do so by simply inserting a “fake” signed_attestation (with the correct source_epoch and target_epoch numbers), and a “fake” signed_block (with the correct slot number). Yes. Teku doesn’t record each individual attestation and block signed to keep the slashing protection as simple as possible. So it can only produce the minimal format. Have some questions, DMing you on TG Vouch also uses the minimal style

excerpts.content:
Are any of the clients using the `minimal` style of slashing DB for slashing protection? `minimal` meaning only storing the latest attestation & block that was signed, as defined here: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3076#rationale
> Whilst the format outlined in this specification is most similar to the old complete, clients who wish to follow a simpler slashing protection strategy (i.e. the old minimal), can do so by simply inserting a “fake” signed_attestation (with the correct source_epoch and target_epoch numbers), and a “fake” signed_block (with the correct slot number).

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: Yes. Teku doesn’t record each individual attestation and block signed to keep the slashing protection as simple as possible. So it can only produce the minimal format.
